title: Make the String Great
prompt: A string is called "good" if it does not contain two adjacent characters that are the same letter but with opposite case, e.g. `a` and `A`. Given a string `s`, repeatedly remove such adjacent bad pairs until the string is good, then return the resulting string. The result is guaranteed to be unique.

examples.explanation: Removing "Ee" gives "leetcode", which has no adjacent same-letter opposite-case pairs left.
Removing "bB" gives "aAcC"; removing "aA" gives "cC"; removing "cC" gives "".

constraints: s consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters
hints: Removing a pair can create a brand new adjacent bad pair right where the removal happened — repeatedly rescanning the string is wasteful.
A stack lets you handle cascading removals in a single left-to-right pass.
Push each character; before pushing, check if it forms a bad pair with the stack's current top (same letter, opposite case) — if so, pop instead of pushing.

solution.approach: Process the string left to right with a stack. For each character, check whether it and the stack's top are the same letter in opposite case (checked via case-insensitive equality plus differing case) — if so, pop the top (canceling the pair) instead of pushing the new character. Otherwise push it. Because the stack always reflects the current 'good' prefix, any cascading collapse (a removal exposing a new bad pair) is handled automatically as later characters are processed.
